De-Anne Kelly voted to pass a 2001 gambling law that banned offshore casinos from accepting Australian customers. (AAP: Alan Porritt)

A German activist has released documents from inside a Caribbean gambling regulator.

The leak revealed De-Anne Kelly's past involvement with LuckyBet casino.

Ms Kelly had argued in support of the Interactive Gambling Act decades before LuckyBet was warned about allegedly contravening it.

Howard-era minister De-Anne Kelly has been revealed as a co-founder and former part-owner of LuckyBet, an online casino registered in the Caribbean.

LuckyBet was formally warned by the communications regulator for allegedly contravening an Australian gambling law in September last year, after Ms Kelly had ceased to hold a stake in the company.

Decades earlier, Ms Kelly had voted to pass the Interactive Gambling Act (IGA).
